- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates in the final 5–10 days, particularly after a spike in the middle of the forecast horizon.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values when recent history includes a sharp decline (e.g., 66–67 range) followed by a rebound.
- Underreacts to sustained upward momentum in the 30-day history; fails to fully capture the mean-reversion effect when prices are above 70.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after a significant spike.
- Overestimates volatility in the early forecast window, leading to overly conservative (low) forecasts for the first 5 days.
- When true price rises above 72, model often fails to sustain the peak, underestimating the continuation or overestimating the decline.
- Shows strong bias toward smoothing out short-term volatility, underestimating sharp reversals or sudden spikes in the last 5–7 days.
